translations.title: How can a few contact-timing constraints train several biped gaits without joint-by-joint reference motion?
translations.answer: Periodic rewards use phase, duty factor, and relative leg phase to compose desired foot-force and swing-velocity timing for standing, walking, running, hopping, and related gaits without copying every joint trajectory. They specify contact rhythm only; phase mismatch, foot slip, impact, torque, and hardware safety still require independent constraints and validation.
translations.applicability.assumptions.0: A periodic phase variable and desired contact rhythm are meaningful for the target gait.
translations.applicability.assumptions.1: Torque, impact, posture, and slip are checked outside the contact clock.
translations.applicability.environments.0: Periodic standing, walking, running, hopping, and gait-transition tasks
translations.applicability.robots.0: Cassie in the paper; other bipeds require new phase, reward, and hardware validation
translations.applicability.simulators.0: MuJoCo/Cassie simulation used by the paper and pinned APEX implementation
translations.confidence_rationale: The paper equations and phase/contact figures define the reward semantics, hardware experiments demonstrate multiple Cassie gaits, and the pinned code exposes the same clock-based interface. Confidence is capped because gait timing, actuation, and transfer bounds are platform-specific.
translations.evidence.0.note: Defines smooth periodic force/velocity coefficients, composes multiple gait rhythms, and reports simulated and real Cassie results.
translations.evidence.0.title: Sim-to-Real Learning of All Common Bipedal Gaits via Periodic Reward Composition
translations.evidence.1.note: Shows the official simulator and phase-clock reward path used for periodic-gait training and evaluation.
translations.evidence.1.title: osudrl/apex official implementation
